analysis.investment_thesis: Campus Activewear is a genuinely good business with ~32% ROCE, but at an EV of ~INR 7,788 Cr against EBIT of only INR 183 Cr, the earnings yield is a paltry 2.4% — far below the 12% minimum the Magic Formula demands. A great business at a terrible price is still a bad investment.
key_strengths: High ROCE of ~31.8% — clears the Magic Formula's 25%+ excellence threshold, indicating genuine competitive returns on capital.
Consistent OCF generation: 5/5 years positive, with FCF of INR 176–219 Cr in the last two years — asset-light shoe brand economics.
Dominant mass-market sports footwear brand with 72% promoter skin-in-the-game and a wide distribution moat in Tier 2/3 India.
key_risks: Earnings yield of ~2.4% (EBIT INR 183 Cr / EV ~INR 7,788 Cr) is catastrophically low by Magic Formula standards — priced for perfection.
Revenue and operating income have stalled/declined from their 2022–2023 peaks (Op. income: INR 242 Cr in 2022 → INR 183 Cr in 2025), undermining the growth premium baked into the 55x P/E.
Intensifying competition from Nike, Adidas, and Indian rivals (Bata, Liberty) in the mass-sports segment could compress already-thin operating margins (14.9%).
red_flags: Earnings yield ~2.4% — roughly 5x below the Magic Formula's minimum attractive threshold of 12%.
Operating income peaked in 2022 at INR 242 Cr and has not recovered — raises questions about earnings quality and cyclicality at this valuation.
EV/EBITDA of 33x and P/E of 55.7x for a business with flat revenue growth (INR 1,484 Cr in 2023 vs. INR 1,593 Cr in 2025 = ~7% over 2 years) is unjustifiable under any value framework.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Campus Activewear yields a stark verdict: excellent business quality, terrible price. EBIT of INR 183 Cr (FY2025) against an enterprise value of ~INR 7,788 Cr (market cap INR 7,573 Cr + debt INR 232 Cr − cash INR 17 Cr) gives an earnings yield of just 2.4% — less than a fifth of my 12% minimum. On the other side of the formula, ROCE of ~31.8% is genuinely excellent and clears the 25%+ bar for "good business." But the Magic Formula explicitly requires both metrics to rank highly simultaneously. When only one leg is strong, the formula says pass.

What makes this especially painful to avoid is that the business fundamentals are legitimate: consistent cash generation (OCF positive all 5 years), a recognizable brand, and a structurally underpenetrated Indian sports footwear market. However, operating income peaked at INR 242 Cr in FY2022, dipped to INR 143 Cr in FY2024, and has only partly recovered to INR 183 Cr in FY2025 — yet the market still prices it at 55x earnings. The market is paying a growth premium for a business that is currently growing revenue at ~7% over two years. Until the price corrects toward an earnings yield of 10–12% (implying a price of roughly INR 70–85, all else equal), this stock does not make the Magic Formula screen.
